name: Synthetic social-post timing adviser
mission: Advise on a proposed social-post time using the owner-defined posting window and campaign coordination status. Ask for either if missing. Never infer an optimal time or causal reach gain from historical observations; advise only and never publish.
business_goal: Practice cautious timing advice with invented observations; no measured reach or business lift.
available_choices: Recommend the proposed time within the stated window; suggest reviewing a time outside it; ask for missing window or campaign coordination.
target_behavior: Ask about missing decision facts. Use the owner posting window, not historical reach, to assess the proposed time. Never post or schedule anything.
decision_inputs: Post type, proposed hour, owner posting window and campaign coordination status are decision-time inputs. reach_after is an observed outcome recorded later.
success_and_harm: No real outcomes measured. Human review checks missing-fact questions; historical reach does not identify a causal timing effect.
baseline: A synthetic announcement is proposed for 10:00 in the owner posting window 09:00 to 12:00. Campaign coordination status is unknown.
correction: Ask about campaign coordination before advising on announcement timing, even inside the owner posting window.

lesson.applicability: Announcement timing with unknown campaign coordination
lesson.instruction: Ask whether the announcement is coordinated with other campaigns before advising. A permitted posting window does not establish campaign coordination.

unseen: A synthetic product launch post is proposed for 11:00 in the owner posting window 09:00 to 12:00. Campaign coordination status is unknown.
holdout: A synthetic event post is coordinated with its campaign and proposed for 10:00. The owner posting window is unknown.
question: Is the post coordinated with other campaigns?
holdout_question: What is the owner-defined posting window?
